reviewer: OMP agent (M15 development and release images)
note: IMAGE-002 run development image: src/images/container_runtime.zig generates a Dockerfile from the declaration, takes the pinned toolchain from the build context and verifies it against the digest scripts/fetch-zig-linux.sh records, then builds a real Jackage fixture and runs its tests inside the container. Delivering the toolchain from the context rather than re-fetching it inside the image was a decision made from evidence: a download inside the container produced a tarball that failed the very same digest check, and refusing that is far easier than debugging it - the image now needs no network at all. The context is checked to be outside a Windows mount before anything is built, because a build whose filesystem operations travel through the translation layer is exactly what the declared environment exists to avoid. The exit code is load-bearing and tested: a fixture whose test fails makes the same command fail, which matters because Zig's build runner withholds a passing test's output, so a run that reported success for everything would be indistinguishable from one that reported nothing. Evidence is recorded inside the WSL2 guest, so actualPlatform is genuinely linux-x86_64. Fault proof: reporting the container's exit code as success makes the failing-fixture assertion fail (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
